title: Regression Discontinuity with Two Noisy Score Replicates and Unknown Measurement Error
banked_reason: D0.5.G: paper_score_ceiling 7.0 < 7.4, graded tier subfield below field floor; salvageable=false in scope
gap_reasons: The proved minimax match for the outcome trace and jump is confined to β=2 and class constants admitting the Laplace construction; the general ordinary-smooth result is an upper bound.
The fixed compact-spectrum construction rules out polynomial rates but does not establish a sharp modulus.

The inference results cover predetermined finite grids or menus, and the band result requires a lower bound on contrast variance; the package gives no application or numerical evidence for the practical value of those sets under its global smoothness and nondifferential-error assumptions.
D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 7 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'subfield'.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery established latent cutoff trace identification, an ordinary-smooth upper risk bound, a full-class β=2 Laplace minimax match, compact-spectrum no-polynomial separation, and finite-grid/menu weak-fuzzy inference. The field-tier review credited these results but judged the delivered scope subfield: the general-β converse, sharp compact modulus, broader inference, and practical validation remain outside this run. Schennach2004ET primary theorem text was inaccessible; comparisons use an identified secondary restatement and disclose that limit.
tldr: With true assignment side and two independent noisy score replicates, marked/unmarked transform cancellation identifies and estimates latent-cutoff outcome and receipt traces despite unknown, possibly asymmetric channels. The class-uniform ordinary-smooth band estimator has root-MSE order \(n^{-q/(2q+2\beta+1)}\); for every fixed \(q\ge2\), its \(\beta=2\) rate matches a full-class lower bound on the paper's Laplace-admitting \(\mathcal P_{q,2}\), even with both error laws revealed. The results also give fixed compact-band no-polynomial separation and bias-aware finite-grid and finite-menu sharp and weak-fuzzy inference under the stated global smoothness and nondifferentiality conditions.
gap: Repeated-measurement Fourier cancellation, nonparametric pointwise regression, zero-robust identification under other tail conditions, known-error RD estimation, and observed-score weak-fuzzy inversion are established. DongOtsuTaylor2025 Section 1.1, PDF pp. 4–5, and Section 3, PDF p. 9, give a published secondary account of Schennach2004ET’s two-score model, Fourier estimator, polynomial/logarithmic pointwise normal rates, and normal/Laplace examples. EcklesIgnatiadisWagerWu2020 PDF p. 1 and Assumptions 1–2 on pp. 3–4 instead assign treatment from the observed noisy score and use known \(p(Z\mid U)\); pp. 13–14 show external repeat-based calibration. These accessible statements leave the proposed class-uniform one-sided marked endpoint bound, full two-replicate Laplace converse, fixed compact-spectrum endpoint separation, and associated RD inference unresolved. Schennach2004ET’s primary theorem pages were inaccessible, so this is a scoped comparison to the secondary restatement, without priority or rate-domination claims.
fill: Establish a uniform endpoint upper bound and a matching full two-replicate Laplace lower bound, then prove a fixed compact-band no-polynomial separation and honest trace-based sharp/fuzzy confidence sets.
